Rick can iron 4 dress shirts in an hour.  He can iron 3 dress pants in an hour.  If he spends 3 hours ironing dress shirts and 5 hours ironing dress pants, how many pieces of clothing has he ironed?

Given:
- Rick irons 4 dress shirts per hour.
- Rick irons 3 dress pants per hour.
- He spends 3 hours ironing dress shirts.
- He spends 5 hours ironing dress pants.

To find:
- Total number of pieces of clothing ironed.

Operations:
1. Calculate the number of dress shirts ironed: \(4 \text{ shirts/hour} \times 3 \text{ hours} = 12 \text{ shirts}\).
2. Calculate the number of dress pants ironed: \(3 \text{ pants/hour} \times 5 \text{ hours} = 15 \text{ pants}\).
3. Add the number of shirts and pants to get the total: \(12 \text{ shirts} + 15 \text{ pants} = 27 \text{ pieces of clothing}\).

Final: 27
